MODT.name: Model Texture Hashes
MODT.note: The model's texture hashes. Fallout 4's MODT comes in three forms, told by the version word at the head: version 2 is three words and nothing else, version 3 is a 16-byte header and then the entries, and version 4 is a 20-byte header and then the entries. Each entry is 12 bytes: a hash, the "dds" extension and a second hash. [measured: of the 19,354 MODT fields in Fallout4.esm, 66 are version 2, 791 are version 3 and 18,497 are version 4; every version-3 field is 16 bytes plus a whole number of twelve-byte entries, and every version-4 field is 20 bytes plus a whole number of them.]

union.name: Version 2
union.note: The oldest form: three words and no entries at all. [measured: 66 MODT fields in Fallout4.esm have this version, and every one of them is twelve bytes.]

union.name: Version 3
union.note: The older form: a 16-byte header and then the entries, one per texture. [measured: 791 MODT fields in Fallout4.esm have this version; every one is 16 bytes plus a multiple of twelve.]

union.name: Version 4
union.note: The current form: a 20-byte header and then the entries. [measured: 18,497 MODT fields in Fallout4.esm have this version; every one is 20 bytes plus a multiple of twelve, and the entry count is the header's count plus its materials count in all but two.]

struct.name: unique_textures
struct.note: How many distinct textures the model's materials use.

struct.name: materials
struct.note: How many materials the model has. The number of entries that follow is this count plus the header's own count.

struct.name: entries
struct.note: The model's texture entries. They fill the rest of the field, which is always a whole number of them: the entry count is the header's count plus its materials count, and the field's length confirms it. [measured: 18,495 of the 18,497 version-4 MODT fields in Fallout4.esm are 20 bytes plus a whole number of twelve-byte entries, and the count matches the header's count plus its materials count.]

struct.name: extension
struct.note: The texture's extension, four bytes: usually "dds" and a NUL, but not always. [measured: the extension is not a NUL-terminated string in every entry — some hold other bytes.]

struct.name: second_hash
struct.note: A second hash, whose meaning is not documented.
